display.purpose: The page's one headline and the closing band's head. Barlow Condensed 700, uppercase, balanced wrap.

body.purpose: All of the product's own prose, in Archivo, capped by role between 40ch and 64ch.

quote.purpose: The inspected document's own words: source sentences, hedges, counter-offer wording. Spectral only, never below reading size.

label.purpose: Citations, key label, column minors, sheet number. Condensed caps at 0.11em.

micro-label.purpose: Title-block and schedule-band field names, the smallest lettering on the sheet.

figure.purpose: Any number a reader might compare, locate or count. Tabular numerals via .tnum.

op-display.purpose: Operate step 10 (2.125rem). The document name in the head bar, the intake head, the all-clear stamp. Barlow Condensed 700, uppercase. Fixed rem, never clamped.

op-headline.purpose: Operate step 9 (1.75rem). Section heads on a task surface. Barlow Condensed 700 uppercase, drops to step 8 below 48rem.

op-title.purpose: Operate step 8 (1.375rem). Flag number, clause type, panel title, query refusal. The thing a reader scans for.

op-quote.purpose: Operate step 7 (1.25rem). The source sentence in Spectral 400 at 1.45 — still the largest reading size in the flag body.

op-lead.purpose: Operate step 6 (1.125rem). Summary prose, the asked question, a red-line entry, a library document name, the counter-offer wording.

op-body.purpose: Operate step 5 (1rem). The base size: interface prose in Archivo 400/1.55, button lettering in Barlow Condensed 600, the document panel's clauses in Spectral.

op-body-sm.purpose: Operate step 4 (0.9375rem). Secondary and supporting prose, panel leads, notes, metadata values.

op-minor.purpose: Operate step 3 (0.875rem). Severity and threshold rank names, small buttons, clause references, captions, footnotes.

op-label.purpose: Operate step 2 (0.8125rem). Condensed caps labels at 0.10–0.11em: citations, panel statuses, field labels, counts.

op-micro.purpose: Operate step 1 (0.75rem). Head-bar field names only — the smallest lettering on a task surface.

knownIssues.name: font-path-port-obstruction
knownIssues.detail: All six faces are loaded from ../landing/fonts/*.woff2. That relative path resolves only in the static two-folder build and breaks the moment this surface becomes app/workspace/page.tsx. The faces must move to public/fonts/ or next/font/local as part of the port. Recorded, not fixed.

knownIssues.name: leader-and-caret-omitted
knownIssues.detail: The workspace source figure keeps the lift ground, the 2px mark-orange top rule and the ruled citation line, but drops the leader-and-caret form and the --source-pad derived clearance that DESIGN.md names as an authored form of this world. A deviation from the incumbent system, not a new Operate rule. The Derived Clearance Rule still stands.

knownIssues.name: severity-swatch-size-drift
knownIssues.detail: 2.1 x 1.4rem against the recorded 2.25 x 1.5rem, and the key does not enlarge the swatch as the Persuade key does (3.25 x 1.7rem). The recorded system values are unchanged; the workspace numbers are drift and are not canonized.

knownIssues.name: library-selection-rule-weight
knownIssues.detail: The current-row left rule is declared at 2px and then overridden to 1px by a later duplicate border-left-width declaration, so the selection reads thinner than the flag row's 2px selection rule. Reported, not repaired; the 2px selection weight is the system value.

knownIssues.name: untokenized-white
knownIssues.detail: Pure white appears as the literal #fff on the primary button label, the open flag's source figure and the cited clause, while the palette already carries it as field-ink. Cosmetic inconsistency in the source, not a second colour.

components.name: Threshold Mark
components.description: A solid mark-orange square with a 1px charcoal border, deliberately never hatched: hatch density means severity rank, and a threshold is not a rank. It is the reader's own declared unacceptable term, disqualifying however the clause would otherwise rank. Full size (1.1rem) in flag bodies, the red-lines panel and the key; small (0.8rem) on collapsed flag rows and scope rows so a match is visible before the flag is opened.
components.html:
Matches one of your red lines: “I will not give a personal guarantee.”

§ 12.4

components.name: Side Panel
components.description: The reader's red lines, their library and their own document open as a right-edge panel over a scrim: role=dialog, aria-modal, Tab trapped inside, Escape closes, focus returns to the opener, and body scroll locks. Bordered with a 1.5px charcoal rule, drawn and not raised. Full width below 48rem.
components.html:
Your red lines

Terms you will not accept, in your own words. A match is disqualifying however that clause would otherwise rank.
components.css: .ds-panel-scrim { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: var(--scrim, rgba(25,27,29,0.28)); } .ds-panel { position: absolute; inset-block: 0; right: 0; width: min(24rem, 100%); background: var(--bar, #e4e8e6); border-left: 1.5px solid var(--ink, #191b1d); border-radius: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-panel-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.85rem 1.1rem 0.75rem; border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--ink, #191b1d); } .ds-panel-title { margin: 0; font-family: "Barlow Condensed", Archivo, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.375rem; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.01em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-panel-close { background: none; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #9aa3a1); border-radius: 0; color: var(--ink, #191b1d); padding: 0.35rem; display: flex; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 170ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-panel-close:hover { background: var(--sheet-lift, #f6f7f7); border-color: var(--ink, #191b1d); } .ds-panel-close:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--orange-mark, #e0521c); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-panel-body { padding: 1.1rem; overflow-y: auto; } .ds-panel-lead { margin: 0; font: 400 0.9375rem/1.55 Archivo, sans-serif; color: var(--ink-2, #4d5553); max-width: 60ch; }

components.name: Library Row
components.description: One saved document per hairline-ruled row, the whole row a button: name, metadata, and its own expiry, with an expiring document's date in deep orange ink. The current document carries a mark-orange left rule and the lift ground. Orange job two of three.
components.css: .ds-lib { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; border-top: 1.5px solid var(--ink, #191b1d); } .ds-lib-item { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #c4cbc9); } .ds-lib-open { width: 100%; display: grid; gap: 0.15rem; text-align: left; background: none; border: 0; border-left: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; padding: 0.75rem 0.6rem; font: 400 1rem/1.55 Archivo, sans-serif; color: var(--ink, #191b1d); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 170ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-lib-open:hover { background: var(--sheet-lift, #f6f7f7); } .ds-lib-open:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--orange-mark, #e0521c); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-lib-item--current .ds-lib-open { border-left-color: var(--orange-mark, #e0521c); background: var(--sheet-lift, #f6f7f7); } .ds-lib-name { font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.125rem; } .ds-lib-meta, .ds-lib-exp { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--ink-3, #5f6765); } .ds-lib-exp--soon { color: var(--orange-ink, #a83513); font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Analysing State
components.description: Waiting is named, not spun: three checkbox-square steps that advance one at a time (extracting, checking clause types, matching red lines) over panel-grey skeleton bars. The active step's square fills mark orange, a finished one fills green. The pulse runs only when motion is welcome.

components.css: .ds-steps { list-style: none; margin: 0 0 1.5rem; padding: 0; max-width: 40rem; } .ds-step { padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #c4cbc9); font: 400 0.9375rem/1.55 Archivo, sans-serif; color: var(--ink-3, #5f6765); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem; } .ds-step::before { content: ""; width: 0.85rem; height: 0.85rem; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #9aa3a1); border-radius: 0; flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-step--active { color: var(--ink, #191b1d); } .ds-step--active::before { background: var(--orange-mark, #e0521c); border-color: var(--ink, #191b1d); } .ds-step--done { color: var(--ink-2, #4d5553); } .ds-step--done::before { background: var(--green, #1d6b4c); border-color: var(--ink, #191b1d); } .ds-skel-wrap { display: grid; gap: 0.7rem; max-width: 60rem; } .ds-skel { display: block; height: 1rem; background: var(--panel, #e1e5e3); } .ds-skel--wide { height: 2rem; max-width: 28rem; } .ds-skel--row { height: 3rem; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-skel { animation: ds-pulse 1400ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) infinite alternate; } } @keyframes ds-pulse { from { opacity: 0.55; } to { opacity: 1; } }

narrative.overview:
Redline looks like the document a surveyor hands you before you commit: a dilapidations report, a schedule of defect. One dyeline sheet, bound at its left edge by a hatched margin rule, carrying a numbered schedule of flags in charcoal ink. Every element is a ruled row on that sheet. Nothing floats, nothing is a card, nothing is tilted into perspective, and the product's own interface is never screenshotted as an image of itself — the document is the stage, at full scale.

The register is measured and forensic rather than alarming. Safety orange is the only warm thing on the page and it is Committed: it owns two whole regions, bleeding to the sheet's edges, and appears nowhere as a decorative accent. Severity is stated twice — a named rank in condensed caps plus a diagonal hatch whose density carries the same information — so the page never asks a reader to decode a colour. Absence is drawn as deliberately as presence: the inspection scope, the all-clear stamp, and the limitations list get the same rule weight and the same type ramp as the flags do.

This is a single committed light world. color-scheme: light is declared and there is no dark variant; the use scene is daytime, a browser, and a client waiting on a signature, not a category habit about near-black hero sections. The page refuses the arrangement this category ships: no near-black hero, no perspective app screenshot, no three-card icon row, no ranking by how common a clause is.
keyCharacteristics: One sheet, ruled rows, zero cards and zero corner radius.
Charcoal ink on a cool dyeline ground; orange owns regions, never accents.
Severity double-encoded: named rank plus hatch density.
Three type voices, strictly separated — the survey's lettering never shares a face with the document's own words.
Flat by construction: no shadows anywhere, depth from rule weight and a single tonal lift.
One authored motion moment, entirely from an already-visible default.
Two densities, one world: a Persuade sheet on clamped display type, an Operate sheet on a fixed ten-step rem ramp.
At Operate density orange has exactly three jobs — primary action, current selection, severity and threshold marks — and no authored entrance.

rules.name: The Two-Value Orange Rule
rules.body: The orange is two values on purpose. Marks, rules, hatch, focus ring and caret use the contract's safety orange; the two whole-region committed fields step down to the deeper field orange, because white and every legible tint of white fail 4.5:1 on the safety value. This is contrast-forced, not taste, and is cited at source in landing/redline.css:21–24. Never unify them, and never set white text on the mark value.

rules.name: The Committed Field Rule
rules.body: Orange arrives as a region or not at all — a full-bleed band with lettering inside it. It is never a scattered accent, never a tint wash, never a border colour on a neutral row. On this Persuade surface there are exactly two such fields. On task surfaces at Operate density the same world narrows to Restrained: orange is permitted only on the primary action, the current selection, and severity marks. Those tokens now exist: the workspace build created the Operate layer recorded in this file (bar, field-bg, disabled-ink, scrim, and the fixed ten-step rem ramp). Extend that layer for a new task surface; do not re-derive one from the Persuade ramp.

rules.name: The No-Tint-Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Inside an orange field, hierarchy comes from size, weight and tracking — never from a lighter tint of the field colour, because no tint light enough to read clears 4.5:1 against it. Label and value both sit at pure white and are told apart by 0.75rem/0.13em condensed caps against 1rem medium sentence case.

rules.name: The Double-Encoded Severity Rule
rules.body: Severity is always a named rank and a hatch density; colour is never the sole signal. The ranks are Highest, High and Medium — and only those words. "Category" is reserved for clause type in this product and must never number a severity.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The survey's lettering and the document's voice never share a face. Barlow Condensed and Archivo belong to Redline; Spectral belongs to the inspected document and to nothing else. That separation is the mechanism by which a reader can always tell the product's words from the document's words — legibility of authorship, not decoration — and it carries unchanged into the app shell.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any figure a reader might compare, locate or count carries .tnum. A clause reference set in proportional numerals is a defect.

rules.name: The Caps-Are-Structural Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to Barlow Condensed — headings, ranks, labels. Archivo body prose and Spectral quotations are never capitalised or letterspaced for emphasis.

rules.name: The Derived Clearance Rule
rules.body: The source figure's leader lives in its left gutter, so that gutter is a local custom property (--source-pad) the leader positions against. Clearance around a mark is derived from one declared value, never eyeballed twice.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Raised Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn, never lifted. A new surface that needs a boundary gets a rule at the weight its level deserves; one that needs to feel closer gets the tonal lift or a hatch. Never a shadow, never a glow, never a backdrop blur.

rules.name: The Already-Visible Rule
rules.body: Every animation begins from a state in which the content is already visible and readable. Nothing content-bearing is ever clipped, hidden or faded from zero by motion, and no text depends on a keyframe running to be legible. An earlier revision of this build hid the source sentence when the animation did not run; that is the failure this rule exists to prevent. Test: disable JS and CSS animation — every word must still be on the page.

rules.name: The Open-Without-JS Rule
rules.body: Without JavaScript every flag is open and fully readable. JS only adds the collapse behaviour and the one-open-at-a-time discipline. Disclosure is an enhancement; it is never the condition of reading the evidence.

rules.name: The Fixed-Ramp-At-Operate Rule
rules.body: Operate surfaces use a fixed rem ramp of exactly ten steps — 0.75, 0.8125, 0.875, 0.9375, 1, 1.125, 1.25, 1.375, 1.75, 2.125rem — and no clamp. Fluid display sizes belong to the Persuade sheet, where the headline is the composition; a heading that breathes inside a panel at a fixed desktop DPI looks worse, not better. Ten is the consolidated count: the first workspace build sprawled to roughly sixteen distinct sizes and that was drift, not a system. A new Operate size is added by consolidating two existing ones, never by appending an eleventh.

rules.name: The Three-Jobs Rule
rules.body: At Operate density orange has exactly three jobs: the primary action, the current selection, and severity or threshold marks. The current selection is drawn as a 2px mark-orange bottom rule on the open flag row and a mark-orange left rule on the current library row. Deep Orange Ink additionally carries links and small status lettering, as the Persuade surface already sanctions. Everything else on a task surface is ink, rule and ground.

rules.name: The Threshold-Is-Not-A-Rank Rule
rules.body: A severity mark is hatched; a threshold mark is a solid mark-orange block with a 1px charcoal border and is never hatched. Hatch density encodes rank, and a threshold has no rank — it is the reader's own declared unacceptable term, disqualifying however the clause would otherwise rank. The two marks never merge, never share a shape, and the threshold never sits in the rank rows of the key: it spans beneath them under its own rule.

rules.name: The Scrim-Is-Not-A-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A panel is separated from the sheet by a 1.5px charcoal rule on its leading edge and a flat 28% ink scrim over everything behind it. The scrim is a dimmed ground, not a cast shadow: it has no blur, no offset and no spread, and it never gains one. There is still no box-shadow, filter or backdrop-filter anywhere in this system.

rules.name: The No-Entrance-At-Operate Rule
rules.body: The strike — the landing page's authored five-beat entrance — is Persuade-only and is deliberately absent from task surfaces. Operate motion is functional and short: 170ms on a state change, 200ms on a disclosure chevron, a stepped named progress list and a pulsing skeleton while real work happens. A task surface never performs its own arrival.

dos: Do build every new block as a ruled row or ruled cell on the one sheet, boundaries drawn with the hairline (1px {colors.rule}) and section breaks with 1.5px solid {colors.ink}.
Do use the mark orange for marks, rules, hatch, caret and focus, and the field orange for whole regions with white lettering on them — and keep both values as they are.
Do encode severity twice: a named rank in Barlow Condensed caps plus a hatch swatch at one of the three published duty cycles (4/7, 2/9, 1/12).
Do name the ranks Highest, High and Medium, and use the product's own words elsewhere too — a flag, its source sentence, an all-clear, a clause type.
Do set every quoted sentence and every hedge in Spectral, and everything the product itself says in Archivo or Barlow Condensed.
Do carry .tnum on every figure a reader might compare or locate.
Do derive clearance around a mark from a declared custom property, as the source figure derives its gutter from --source-pad.
Do theme browser surfaces — selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring — from the palette on any new page.
Do start every animation from an already-visible, already-readable default, and make the page complete without JavaScript.
Do narrow orange to primary action, current selection and severity marks on Operate-density task surfaces, keeping this palette and these three faces.

Do set Operate surfaces on the fixed ten-step rem ramp (0.75 / 0.8125 / 0.875 / 0.9375 / 1 / 1.125 / 1.25 / 1.375 / 1.75 / 2.125rem), and earn a new step by consolidating two, never by appending an eleventh.

Do mark a threshold match with a solid orange block and a 1px charcoal border — full size (1.1rem) in flag bodies, the red-lines panel and the key; small (0.8rem) on any collapsed row, so the match is visible before the flag is opened.
Do hold Operate motion functional: 170ms on a state change, 200ms on a disclosure chevron, a named stepped wait, and no authored entrance.
Do make an overlay accountable: role=dialog, aria-modal, Tab trapped inside it, Escape closing it, focus returned to whatever opened it, and body scroll locked while it is open.
Do carry .tnum onto task surfaces too — flag numbers, clause references, counts, dates and expiries — and keep a screen-reader-only .u-sr sentence beside every mark that carries meaning.
donts: Don't introduce a card, a rounded panel, or a nested container. Radius is 0 everywhere in this system.
Don't add a box-shadow, glow or backdrop blur to convey depth. Use rule weight, the single tonal lift, or hatch density.
Don't build hierarchy inside an orange field from a lighter tint of that orange — no tint that reads clears 4.5:1. Use size, weight and tracking.
Don't scatter orange as a decorative accent, a tint wash, or a border on a neutral row. It owns a region or it is a mark.
Don't let colour alone carry severity, and don't render severity as a smooth gradient.
Don't use "finding" for a flag, "red line" for a threshold outside the interface label "your red lines", or "category" for anything but clause type.
Don't set a source sentence smaller than the surrounding prose, truncate it, soften its wording, or let any animation or collapse state hide it.
Don't add a fourth type family, and don't set the product's own lettering in Spectral or the document's quoted words in Archivo or Barlow Condensed.
Don't load fonts from a third-party host or fall back to a system display face; all three families are self-hosted woff2 with font-display: swap.
Don't add a dark variant. This is a single committed light world (color-scheme: light) chosen from the use scene; there is no dark counterpart to inherit.
Don't invent app-shell tokens. The Restrained step-down has landed as the recorded Operate layer — extend it, and don't re-derive a task surface from the Persuade ramp.
Don't clamp a font size on an Operate surface, and don't carry the Persuade clamped display ramp into a task frame. Fixed rem, ten steps.
Don't hatch a threshold mark, rank it, or let it share a shape with a severity swatch. Hatch means rank; a threshold has none.
Don't replay the strike, or any authored entrance, on a task surface. Operate motion is 170–200ms and functional.
Don't let the panel scrim acquire a blur, offset or spread, and don't reach for a shadow when a panel needs separating — it gets a 1.5px charcoal rule.
Don't spend orange on an Operate surface outside its three jobs. A hover state, a border on a neutral row, a background tint: all of those are ink, rule or ground.
